headline: Federal judge calls Flock indiscriminate mass surveillance
summary: A federal judge ruled a deputy violated Fourth Amendment rights by using Flock Safety without a warrant, calling it 'indiscriminate mass surveillance'.
details: A federal judge has ruled that a Tulsa sheriff's deputy violated a woman's Fourth Amendment rights by using Flock Safety technology to search for her license plate without a warrant. While this ruling does not set a binding precedent, it is one of the first times a federal judge has deemed a Flock search unconstitutional.

Judge Sara Hill stated the deputy should have obtained a warrant before accessing the Flock database, as there was no apparent reason for the search beyond the vehicle having a California license plate. The deputy then used the woman's travel history from Flock to justify searching her car, where 91 pounds of meth were allegedly found.

Judge Hill declared that all evidence obtained after the warrantless Flock search must be suppressed as 'the fruit of a poisonous tree.' She further criticized warrantless searches of the Flock database, explaining that tracking individuals' locations, even in public, becomes constitutionally problematic when law enforcement can 'indiscriminately and passively catalog your whereabouts over an extended period of time.'

The judge described Flock's system as 'indiscriminate mass surveillance,' noting that it is not targeted at a single individual but collects information on all vehicles passing by its cameras. This data is then made available to law enforcement on demand.

This ruling adds to a growing number of critics of Flock technology from across the political spectrum. Several state governments, including Florida and Texas, have announced they will cease using the technology. Additionally, Senator Bernie Sanders introduced the Block Flock Act, aiming to prohibit federal agencies from using automated license plate readers like Flock.

Flock CEO Garretty Langley has called for a compromise between privacy and safety and has apologized to women who have been stalked using the Flock system. Amidst these cancellations, Flock has reportedly offered voluntary employee buyouts to reduce its workforce.
